Introduction.description: Purpose: Explain the purpose of the requirement gathering process, how this document will facilitate the collection and documentation of requirements, and its role in guiding the project.
Scope: Define the scope of the requirement gathering process, including boundaries of what will be covered and what will not. Specify any constraints or limitations.
Target Audience: Identify intended readers such as project managers, stakeholders, developers, and business analysts. Tailor the document to meet their needs.
References: List any relevant documents, standards, or guidelines that are referenced in the requirement gathering process.

Requirement Gathering Process.description: Methodology: Describe the methodology used for gathering requirements, such as interviews, surveys, workshops, observations, or document analysis. Explain the rationale for choosing these methods.

Stakeholder Identification: Identify key stakeholders involved in the requirement gathering process. Include details on their roles, responsibilities, and how they will contribute to the requirements.
Data Collection Techniques: Outline the techniques and tools used to collect requirements, such as questionnaires, interview guides, or prototyping. Include any relevant templates or forms.
Schedule and Milestones: Provide a timeline for the requirement gathering process, including key milestones, deadlines, and deliverables. Define the phases of requirement collection and review.

Requirement Documentation.description: Requirement Categories: Organize requirements into categories such as functional, non-functional, and technical. Define each category and its significance.
Functional Requirements: Detail the specific functions and behaviors the system must exhibit. Include use cases, scenarios, and detailed descriptions.
Non-Functional Requirements: Specify performance, security, usability, and other quality attributes. Include details on system performance, reliability, and user experience.
Technical Requirements: Describe any technical constraints or needs, such as hardware, software, and integration requirements.

Requirement Details: For each requirement, provide detailed information including Requirement ID (unique identifier), Description (clear and concise), Priority (high/medium/low with impact), Source (stakeholder or regulatory standard), and Acceptance Criteria (criteria for accepting as complete).

Requirement Validation.description: Validation Process: Describe the process for validating requirements to ensure they are accurate, complete, and aligned with stakeholder expectations. Include methods such as reviews, walkthroughs, or prototypes.
Feedback Mechanisms: Outline how feedback will be collected from stakeholders and how it will be incorporated into the requirements. Define the process for handling changes and updates.
Approval Process: Detail the process for obtaining formal approval of the requirements from stakeholders. Include any sign-off procedures and documentation.

Risk Management.description: Risk Identification: Identify potential risks related to the requirements gathering process, such as incomplete requirements or conflicting stakeholder needs.
Risk Assessment: Assess the impact and likelihood of each identified risk. Provide a risk management plan to mitigate and address these risks.
Contingency Plans: Outline contingency plans for managing risks that may arise during the requirement gathering process.

Appendices.description: Supporting Documentation: Include any additional documents, templates, or forms used during the requirement gathering process.
Glossary: Define technical terms, acronyms, and jargon used in the document to ensure clarity and understanding.

Document Guidelines.description: Clarity and Conciseness: Ensure the document is clear and concise, avoiding ambiguity and unnecessary complexity.
Consistency: Use consistent terminology and formatting throughout the document to maintain professionalism and ease of understanding.
Review and Approval: Ensure the document is reviewed and approved by relevant stakeholders before finalizing. This helps verify the accuracy and completeness of the requirements.
Version Control: Maintain a version history of the document to track changes and updates. Ensure that the most current version is referenced and used.

Introduction.description: Overview of the Document's Purpose: Provide a summary of the SRS's role in guiding the development team and ensuring a shared understanding among stakeholders, highlighting its importance for the software lifecycle.
Scope of the Software System: Define the project's boundaries, including what will be included and excluded (features, constraints, limitations) to manage expectations and prevent scope creep.
References to Related Documents: List all external documents, standards (EAII standards), guidelines, legal requirements (PDPP), and technical documentation the SRS relies on.
Target Audience: Specify the intended readers (developers, project managers, clients, end-users) and tailor the content to meet their needs.

Business Requirements.description: Problem Statement: Articulate the business problems or challenges (e.g., manual processes, data fragmentation) that the DRRMS aims to address.
Objectives: Outline the goals and expected benefits of the software, describing how it will improve processes, enhance efficiency, and achieve desired outcomes.

System Overview.description: High-Level Architecture: Provide a high-level view of the system's architecture, including major components and their interactions (using diagrams or textual descriptions).
User Roles and Responsibilities: Define the different user roles (e.g., Administrator, Field Officer, Director) within the system, their responsibilities, and the functionalities they will access.
Relationships between Components: Explain how system components interact with each other and with external systems, detailing the flow of data and control.

Functional Requirements.description: Use Cases and Scenarios: Describe use cases and scenarios illustrating how users will interact with the system, including inputs, system responses, and event sequences.
Descriptions of Features: Provide detailed descriptions of each feature, specifying system behavior in response to user inputs or events, including inputs, outputs, and conditions.
Interactions between Users and the System: Detail the user interface and interaction flow, describing how users will engage with the system and the overall user experience.

Non-Functional Requirements.description: Performance Requirements: Specify expected performance criteria such as response times, throughput, and resource utilization under different conditions and workloads.
Reliability and Availability Specs: Outline requirements for system reliability and availability, including uptime, error recovery, and mechanisms for maintaining operations during failures.
Security Measures and Requirements: Describe security features including access controls, encryption, authentication, and other measures to protect data and system functionality.
Usability Considerations: Define requirements related to the UI and overall usability, including design principles, accessibility features, and ease-of-use factors.

System Constraints.description: Hardware Constraints: Specify limitations or requirements for the hardware environment, including minimum specifications, compatibility, and performance impacts.
Software Constraints: Describe limitations or requirements for the software environment, including OS compatibility, dependencies, and selection criteria for tools or frameworks.

Regulatory Compliance Requirements: Strictly adhere to the Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 (Privacy by Design). This mandates conducting Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) for high-risk activities (Art. 47), implementing verifiable consent mechanisms (Art. 6), and ensuring personal data remains within national borders unless the destination country provides equivalent protections (cross-border transfer restrictions). Must align with industry-specific regulations and national digital standards.

Data Requirements.description: Data Entities and Attributes: Identify the data entities within the system and their attributes, providing a comprehensive overview of the types of data handled and their characteristics.
Relationships between Data Entities: Describe the relationships and associations between different data entities, explaining how data elements interact and are related.

Data Storage and Retrieval Requirements: Specify requirements for storage, retrieval, and processing, including database technologies, data formats, and mechanisms for maintaining integrity and security.

Document Guidelines.description: Clarity and Conciseness: Ensure the document is clear and concise, avoiding unnecessary technical jargon to remain accessible to all readers.
Consistency: Use consistent terminology and formatting throughout the document to maintain professionalism and aid comprehension.
Visual Aids: Incorporate diagrams, charts, and tables to enhance understanding and illustrate complex concepts, making the document more engaging and interpretable.

Review and Approval: Ensure the SRS is reviewed and approved by all relevant stakeholders, including legal and data privacy officers. Verify PDPP compliance (specifically cross-border data transfer restrictions) is accurately captured. This approval acts as a mandatory gateway before development begins.
Version Control: Maintain a version history of the document to track changes and updates, ensuring the most current version is always used and referenced.

Introduction.description: Project Overview: Provide a brief summary of the project, including its goals, scope, and key deliverables. Helps readers understand the context and objectives of the software being developed.
Document Purpose: Clearly articulate the purpose of the SAD. Explain why the document is being created and how it will be used throughout the development process.
Document Scope: Define the scope of the analysis, specifying what aspects of the system are covered and any exclusions. Manage expectations and clarify the focus of the document.
Target Audience: Identify primary readers such as developers, project managers, stakeholders, and end-users. Tailor content to meet the needs of these audiences.

References: List relevant documents, standards, or guidelines referenced in the SAD, including industry standards, regulatory requirements (PDPP), or other technical documents that support the analysis.

System Overview.description: System Purpose: Describe the primary objective and intended outcome of the system. Explain why the system is being developed and what problems it aims to solve.
System Functions: Outline the core functions and features of the system. Provide a high-level view of what the system will do and how it will interact with users and other systems.

System Constraints: Identify any limitations or restrictions affecting the system, including technical constraints, resource limitations, or compliance requirements (e.g., PDPP Proclamation No. 1321/2024, cross-border data transfer restrictions).
System Environment: Describe the environment in which the system will operate, including hardware, software, network configurations, and other environmental factors.
System Stakeholders: List and describe key stakeholders involved in the project, including individuals or groups who have an interest in the system's development and outcome.

Requirements Analysis.description: Functional Requirements: Provide a detailed description of the system's functionalities and behaviors, including specific actions the system must perform and how it will respond to user inputs and system events.

Non-Functional Requirements: Specify performance, security, usability, and other quality attributes. Define how well the system performs its functions, including response times, reliability, and user experience.
User Interface Requirements: Describe the characteristics and design of the user interface, including look and feel, usability considerations, and accessibility features.

Data Requirements: Define the data elements, structures, and relationships within the system, including data storage, retrieval, processing requirements, and data integrity and security considerations.

System Design.description: Architectural Design: Outline the overall architecture of the system, including major components and their interactions. Provide a blueprint for how the system will be structured and how components will work together.
Data Design: Specify the data models and database design, including details on how data will be organized, stored, and accessed within the system.
Interface Design: Define the interfaces between system components and external systems, including specifications for APIs, data exchange formats, and integration points.
Component Design: Detail the design of individual system components, including specific functionalities, interfaces, and interactions of each component within the system.

Analysis Results.description: Feasibility Study: Assess the project's technical, economic, and operational feasibility to evaluate if the project is viable given its constraints and requirements.

Risk Assessment: Identify potential risks and proposed mitigation strategies. For systems involving Machine Learning (ML), include specific AI Risk Assessments to identify potential algorithmic failures and biases.

Ethical AI Review: Conduct a formal analysis of the system's alignment with the National AI Policy. Evaluate the system for bias prevention, fairness, and transparency to ensure AI outcomes do not discriminate against specific groups or reflect historical prejudices.
Alternative Solutions: Explore different design options, technologies, or methodologies to achieve project goals.
Recommendations: Provide suggested actions or decisions based on the analysis results.

Appendices.description: Supporting Documentation: Include any additional relevant information that supports the SAD, such as detailed diagrams, charts, tables, or supplementary documents.
Glossary: Define technical terms and acronyms used in the document to ensure clarity and understanding for all readers, especially those who may not be familiar with specific terminology.

Document Guidelines.description: Clarity and Conciseness: Use easily understandable language and avoid unnecessary technical jargon.
Consistency: Maintain uniform terminology, formatting, and style throughout the artifact.
Visual Aids: Incorporate diagrams and charts to clarify complex architectural or data concepts.

Review and Approval: Ensure the SAD is reviewed and approved by all relevant stakeholders to verify requirement accuracy. For systems processing personal data or employing AI, mandatory review and approval must be sought from the Ethiopian Communications Authority or the designated Data Protection Authority. This ensures compliance with cross-border data transfer restrictions and national safety standards.
Version Control: Maintain a detailed record of revisions and updates to ensure the most current version is utilized by the development team.

Code Readability.description: Write as few lines as possible

Standardize Headers.description: The creator's name of the module
Summary of what the module does

Daily Backups.description: Back up the workflow on TFS
Follows a centralized model and is well-established

Commenting.description: Comments accurately reflect the current state

Importing Code.description: Ensuring Clear Pathways for Code Traceability

Readability.description: Use consistent fonts colors and element styles
Ensure consistency in color and typography

Accessibility.description: Provide text alternatives for non-text content
Correctly handle status like hover, focus, active

Responsive Design.description: Implement a simple and navigable menu
Provide ways to help users navigate
Ensure purpose of each link is clear

Error Handling.description: Give users opportunity to make changes

Visual Design and Performance.description: Choose the right file format for images

Mobile Applications UI.description: Use visual cues and clear elements

Accessibility Core.description: Check all text contrast and background combinations
Check that all form inputs, selects, and textareas have labels
Check for empty buttons and links
Check for redundant or missing titles

Performance & Speed.description: Measure overall performance score using Lighthouse
Measure Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) using Lighthouse
Measure Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) using Lighthouse
Measure Total Blocking Time (TBT) using Lighthouse
Measure Time to Interactive (TTI) using Lighthouse

Responsive Design Checklist.description: Test layout on mobile, tablet, desktop
Check interactive elements touch target size
Check essential content visibility on small screens

Standards.description: Version control system set up (e.g., Git)
Automated testing integrated into CI/CD pipeline
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) scripts in use
Monitoring tools implemented and metrics tracked

Certificate & Release Signing.description: Sign release builds with a dedicated release keystore (never a debug certificate)
Store signing keys in a secrets manager or HSM, not in source control or CI logs
Gate CI/CD pipeline to block release artifacts signed with a debug certificate

Manifest & Component Security.description: Explicitly set android:allowBackup (disable or scope with extraction rules)
Set minSdkVersion to a platform version still receiving security updates
Do not export activities, services, receivers, or providers unless required
Protect exported components with an app-defined signature-level permission

Data Storage & Privacy.description: Never write sensitive data to application logs
Avoid storing sensitive data on shared/external storage
Do not copy sensitive data to the system clipboard
Encrypt or avoid writing sensitive data to temporary files
Encrypt sensitive fields before persisting to local databases
Use parameterized queries; never build SQL from raw string concatenation

Cryptography.description: Avoid deprecated/weak hash algorithms (e.g., SHA-1, MD5); use SHA-256 or stronger
Use a cryptographically secure random number generator (e.g., SecureRandom) for security-sensitive values
Never hardcode secrets, API keys, or credentials in source or native binaries

Native Library & Binary Hardening.description: Compile native libraries with stack canary, NX, and PIE protections
Enable FORTIFY_SOURCE and RELRO for native (non-Dart/Flutter) libraries where supported
Document and justify any anti-VM/anti-emulator (Build.*) fingerprinting logic

Permissions & Malware Patterns.description: Request only the minimum permissions required for a documented feature
Individually justify any permission matching known malware-abused patterns
Scope SMS/CALL_LOG-adjacent or other sensitive content-URI access to the minimum required

Integration Testing.input: Inputs from Module A and B
